# Spec: codec-export C4 — VP9 (libvpx) in WebM, 8-bit SDR and Profile 2 HDR (#377)

## Goal
Add a `vp9_webm` export row: libvpx v1.17.0 (good, cpu-used 4, row-mt; CX-3) encoding into the core's WebM writer with C3's Opus, silent movie, chapters, range and #337 length. It is Profile 0 8-bit for an SDR picture and Profile 2 10-bit for HLG/PQ, with the container's Colour carrying the transfer and HD-5's HDR10. The rate is capped constant quality calibrated against `hevc` / `hevc_10bit`.

## Files
Worktree `~/devel/framejob-codecs` (branch `codecs`). Never commit.
- `designs/spec/11-decisions/codec-export.md`: CX-16 (below), written BEFORE any code. "Amended by CX-16" lines under CX-8 and CX-15 (1)–(3).
- `designs/spec/11-decisions/hdr.md`: "Amended by CX-16" under HD-5's row list (line ~168) and HD-14 (c) (line ~478). There are now six HDR rows and the new sentence.
- `designs/spec/11-decisions/README.md`: the file row's text and line count, plus a CX-16 row. `designs/spec/README.md`: the Lines cells.
- `designs/spec/07.8-export.md`, `07.1-ffi-surface.md` (webm layout comment), `07.4-swift-file-map.md`, `07.10-rust-module-map.md`, `07.9a-agent-tools.md`: the row, the writer, V_VP9.
- `designs/codec-export.md`: a "## C4" record shaped like C3's: decision, what landed, commands and output, calibration, findings, "CLAUDE.md edits owed", owed.
- `core/src/export_encoder.rs`: `Writer::Libvpx` and `Writer::takes_speed`.
- `core/src/export_table.rs`: the `vp9_webm` row; `takes_encoder_speed`; `to_json` (`writer` on every writer row, `encoder_speeds` only where speeds apply).
- `core/src/export.rs`: settings emit `writer` for every writer row and `encoder_speed` only where speeds apply; the module doc.
- `core/src/dynamic_range.rs`: `HDR_ROWS` has six entries, and the 8-bit sentence names `vp9_webm`.
- `core/src/webm_layout.rs`: accepts `V_VP9`, makes the private optional, and checks the depth.
- `core/src/webm_ebml.rs`: `video_entry` takes the codec id and an optional private.
- `core/include/framejob_core.h`: the presets, settings and webm paragraphs.
- `core/tests/export_vp9.rs` (new); `core/tests/webm_writer_vp9.rs` (new, VP9 round trips); `core/tests/common/webm.rs` (hand-built VP9 Profile 0/2 keyframe and inter-frame headers, VP9 layouts); `core/tests/webm_writer_refusals.rs`; `core/tests/export.rs`; `core/tests/export_av1.rs`; `core/tests/export_size.rs`; `core/tests/dynamic_range.rs`; `core/tests/canvas_output.rs`.
- `app/Bridging/FrameJobVPX.h` (new): the shim. `app/Bridging/FrameJob-Bridging-Header.h`: `#include "FrameJobVPX.h"` (quoted, so `swift_build.py` keys it).
- `app/Sources/ExportVideoEncoder.swift` (new): the protocol, the packet and the rate table.
- `app/Sources/ExportVP9Encoder.swift` (new, ≤400 lines): `VP9Encoder`.
- `app/Sources/ExportAV1Encoder.swift`: conforms to the protocol. `Packet` becomes the shared type, and `crf` goes through `ExportRateTable`. The values do not change.
- `app/Sources/ExportEncodePump.swift`: picks the encoder by `settings.writer`. Adds `webmCodec`; `formatDescription` becomes optional.
- `app/Sources/ExportI010.swift` and `app/Resources/Shaders/ExportI010.metal`: the 8-bit I420 kernel and `bitDepth`.
- `app/Sources/ExportAV1Picture.swift`: `cicp`.
- `app/Sources/ExportWebMLayout.swift`: `VideoCodec`; codec id, private, depth.
- `app/Sources/ExportWebMWriter.swift`: the writer guard, the layout call, the doc.
- `app/Sources/ExportPacketSink.swift`: the MP4 sink's format becomes optional.
- `app/Sources/ExporterWriter.swift`: `ExportEncodePump.writer` becomes `.av1Writer` (one identifier).
- `app/Sources/ExportValues.swift`: `ExportPreset.writer` and docs. `app/Sources/ExportSheetOptions.swift`: `codecFactor` takes `vp9`, plus `Applies.softCap`. `app/Sources/ExportSheetResolve.swift` line 477: `applies.softCap`.
- `app/Sources/AgentCatalog+Render.swift`: the descriptions of preset, size (the even list), `video_bitrate` (VP9's soft cap and its measured maximum), `dynamic_range` and `encoder_speed`.
- `tools/proof/vp9_export_proof.py` (new) and `tools/proof/vp9_rate_probe.swift` (new). `tools/proof/export_offset_proof.py` gets E41 and E42: E38/E39 as `vp9_webm`, in `VIDEO_ROWS`, `EXTENSIONS` and the flash preset tuple.
- Re-anchored or with updated sentences: `tools/proof/av1_export_proof.py` (H5's sentence, the `av1-not-hdr` anchor), `tools/proof/webm_export_proof.py` (any anchor this change moves), `tools/proof/hdr_proof.py` (DR sentences), `tools/proof/hevc_alpha_proof.py` (`B6_SIZE`), and `tools/proof/README.md` (a C4 section).
- `tools/proof/work/codec-spike/crf_vp9.py` (new, gitignored): the calibration instrument.
- `docs/guide/export.md`, `docs/guide/hdr-and-color.md`, `docs/guide/mcp.md`, `README.md` (the Export highlight), and `docs/manual-checks.md`. The last gets a new SE-19 (`vp9_webm` in Chrome, Firefox and Safari, 8-bit and an HLG file; Frame Job re-import with picture and sound in sync on another Apple silicon Mac). It also adds `vp9_webm` to HDR-2's row list and HDR-8.

## Interfaces
Core:
- `pub(crate) enum Writer { SvtAv1, Libvpx }`. `as_str`: `"svt_av1"`, `"libvpx"`. `pub(crate) fn takes_speed(self) -> bool` is true for SvtAv1 alone. `Preset::takes_encoder_speed` is `self.writer.is_some_and(Writer::takes_speed)`.
- `const PRESETS: [Preset; 14]`, with `vp9_webm` directly after `av1_webm`: `{id:"vp9_webm", name:"VP9 (WebM)", container: Webm, codec:"vp9", video:true, alpha:false, size:None, fps:None, avf_preset:Some("AVAssetExportPresetPassthrough"), writer:Some(Libvpx)}`. Its presets JSON has `"hdr":true,"writer":"libvpx"` and no `encoder_speeds`.
- Settings for `vp9_webm`: the common keys, plus `alpha` and `writer:"libvpx"` (no `encoder_speed`), plus `color` in an HLG project. `encoder_speed` on it is refused with the existing sentence `vp9_webm has no encoder speed; encoder_speed applies to av1 and av1_webm`.
- `pub(crate) const HDR_ROWS: [&str; 6] = ["hevc_10bit","av1","av1_webm","vp9_webm","prores_422","prores_4444"]`. The sentence is `{id} is 8-bit and writes the SDR version; export dynamic_range "{x}" as hevc_10bit, av1, av1_webm, vp9_webm, prores_422 or prores_4444`.
- `VideoLayout.codec_private_hex: Option<String>` (`#[serde(default)]`). The refusals:
  - `video codec_id "{x}" is not V_AV1 or V_VP9`
  - `the V_AV1 codec_private_hex is empty` (absent or empty)
  - `a V_VP9 track takes no codec_private_hex`
  - `colour bits_per_channel {n} is not 8 or 10`
- `pub(crate) fn video_entry(codec_id: &str, private: Option<&[u8]>, width: u32, height: u32, default_duration_ns: u64, colour: &ColourOut) -> Vec<u8>`. CodecPrivate is written only when `Some`.

Swift:
- `struct ExportEncodedPacket { let data: Data; let pts: Int64; let isLast: Bool; let isKey: Bool }`.
- `protocol ExportVideoEncoder: AnyObject { var name: String { get }; func send(_ frame: I010Frame, index: Int64) throws; func sendEndOfStream() throws; func nextPacket(wait: Bool) throws -> ExportEncodedPacket?; func containerBytes(_ data: Data) throws -> Data }`.
  - `containerBytes` strips TDs for SVT-AV1 and returns VP9's bytes as they are.
  - `nextPacket(wait: true)` answers nil once drained.
- `enum ExportRateTable { static func value(at bitsPerPixel: Double, points: [(bitsPerPixel: Double, value: Double)]) -> UInt32 }`. It interpolates linearly between points and rounds down; beyond either end it answers the end point's value.
- `final class VP9Encoder: ExportVideoEncoder`. `init(width: Int, height: Int, fps: Fps, bitsPerSecond: Int, picture: ExportAV1Picture) throws`; `static func bitDepth(for picture: ExportAV1Picture) -> Int` (8 for `.sdr`, else 10); `static func cqLevel(bitDepth: Int, bitsPerPixel: Double) -> UInt32`.
- `FrameJobVPX.h`:
  - `static inline vpx_codec_err_t framejob_vpx_vp9_enc_init(vpx_codec_ctx_t *ctx, const vpx_codec_enc_cfg_t *cfg, vpx_codec_flags_t flags)` calls `vpx_codec_enc_init(ctx, vpx_codec_vp9_cx(), cfg, flags)`.
  - `static inline vpx_codec_err_t framejob_vpx_control_int(vpx_codec_ctx_t *ctx, int ctrl_id, int value)` calls `vpx_codec_control_`. Swift cannot call that variadic function.
- `I010Frame.bitDepth: Int`. At 8 a sample is one byte (I420); at 10 it is two bytes (I010). Offsets and strides stay in samples. `ExportI010Converter.init(width:height:canvas:fills:picture:bitDepth:pool:)`.
- Metal: `kernel void framejob_export_i420(texture2d<half, access::read> src [[texture(0)]], device uchar *planes [[buffer(0)]], constant ExportI010Uniforms &u [[buffer(1)]], uint2 gid [[thread_position_in_grid]])`.
- `ExportAV1Picture.cicp: (primaries: Int, transfer: Int, matrix: Int)`: sdr 1/1/1, hlg 9/18/9, pq 9/16/9.
- `ExportWebMLayout.VideoCodec { let codecId: String; let codecPrivate: Data?; let primaries: Int; let transfer: Int; let matrix: Int; let bitsPerChannel: Int }`. `Video.codecId`, `Video.codecPrivateHex: String?` and `Colour.bitsPerChannel` become stored values. `init(settings:range:codec: VideoCodec, picture:preSkip:chapters:)`.
- `ExportEncodePump`:
  - `static let av1Writer = "svt_av1"` and `static let vp9Writer = "libvpx"` replace `writer`.
  - `let formatDescription: CMVideoFormatDescription?` is nil on libvpx.
  - `let webmCodec: ExportWebMLayout.VideoCodec`. AV1's comes from `config` at 10 bits; VP9's comes from `picture.cicp` and `bitDepth`.
  - `config` stops being public.
- `ExportMP4PacketSink.init(input: AVAssetWriterInput, format: CMVideoFormatDescription?)`. A nil format makes `append` answer the existing "could not be made a sample" error.
- `ExportPreset.writer: String?` (decoded leniently). `Applies.softCap: Bool { preset?.writer != nil }`.

## Approach
1. **CX-16 first** (default; amends CX-8, CX-15, HD-5, HD-14 (c)):
   1. The row as Interfaces says. It is even-sized, an HDR row, and `optimize_for_network` has no effect on it.
   2. **One speed (CX-3 binds).** cpu-used 4, `VPX_DL_GOOD_QUALITY`, row-mt. There is no `encoder_speeds`, and the Speed popup is disabled on this row. The request's "Speed popup mapped to cpu-used" is not built because it would re-litigate CX-3.
   3. **Depth by picture.** `sdr` (an SDR project, or `sdr` asked) is Profile 0 (`g_profile` 0), 8-bit I420, BT.709. `hlg` and `pq` are Profile 2, 10-bit I010, BT.2020 NCL, with `g_profile` 2, `VPX_CODEC_USE_HIGHBITDEPTH`, `g_bit_depth`/`g_input_bit_depth` 10 and `VPX_IMG_FMT_I42016` (libvpx's `validate_config` refuses a depth above 8 at a profile below 2). Reason: Profile 0 is VP9's universal decode profile, VP9's purpose is web playback (CX-3), and unlike AV1 Main (CX-14 (1)) Profile 0 cannot carry 10 bits. The 8-bit samples are Y = round(16 + 219·Y′) and C = clamp(round(128 + 224·C′), 0, 255), where C′ is the mean of its 2×2 block and the matrix is as CX-14 (3).
   4. **Tags.** `VP9E_SET_COLOR_SPACE` is `VPX_CS_BT_709` or `VPX_CS_BT_2020`, and `VP9E_SET_COLOR_RANGE` is studio. The WebM Colour carries `cicp`, Range 1 and BitsPerChannel 8 or 10. On PQ it also carries HD-5's MasteringMetadata, MaxCLL and MaxFALL. The container is the only transfer label (CX-8).
   5. **No CodecPrivate.** It is optional in Matroska's VP9 mapping, ffmpeg writes none, and #216-R's reader builds `vpcC` from the first keyframe.
   6. **Keys and packets.**
      - `kf_mode` auto, `kf_min_dist` 0, `kf_max_dist` ⌊2·fps⌋.
      - The key flag is `VPX_FRAME_IS_KEY`.
      - `g_lag_in_frames` 25, auto-alt-ref 1, `VP9E_SET_TILE_COLUMNS` 2, frame-parallel 0, `g_threads` set to the active processor count.
      - libvpx packs hidden ARFs into the next shown frame's superframe, so each packet is one shown frame at its pts (timebase 1/fps, pts the index, duration 1).
      - Errors read "libvpx failed: <step> answered <code>: <vpx_codec_error_detail>". For setup failures: "libvpx could not start: …".
   7. **Rate: capped CQ, quality first** (CX-13's model).
      - `rc_end_usage` is `VPX_CQ`, `VP8E_SET_CQ_LEVEL` is the table value, and `rc_target_bitrate` is the cap in kb/s (rounded, at least 1). The cap is the one CX-13 (2) uses.
      - `rc_overshoot_pct` and `rc_undershoot_pct` stay at libvpx's defaults (25/25), as CX-13 took SVT's own default. The Quality tiers' 0.6 factor applies (CX-9 (2)).
      - The table has columns by depth (8 and 10) and points at CX-13's five bits-per-pixel values.
      - The 8-bit column is the lower of two calibrations:
        - (a) The spike's gh5/promo/real8 through the spike's `build/libvpx/vpxenc` (`--end-usage=cq`, the flags above, CQ 10–50 step 2) against `crf.jsonl`'s HEVC rows.
        - (b) The owner's IMG_0018.MOV in an SDR project, exported through a Release copy that reads CQ from a file (`crf_owner.py`'s pattern), against `hevc`. Both are scored against `prores_422` as yuv420p.
      - The 10-bit column comes from the owner clip in an HLG project at `hlg`, against `hevc_10bit` at `hlg`, scored as yuv420p10le.
      - Each cell is the highest CQ reaching at least the comparator's VMAF under the real cap. A cell that misses is lowered by 2 until it meets the comparator or the cap binds.
      - Record every VMAF, the cap shares and the spike clips' maximum cap share in CX-16.
   8. **The shim:** `vpx_codec_enc_init` is a macro and `vpx_codec_control_` is variadic, so the C wrappers live in `FrameJobVPX.h`.
   9. Risks: speed (about 39 fps at 1080p) and the bitrate VP9 needs; Profile 2 player support; HDR rendering not measured; VMAF on HLG; the calibration covers four clips.
2. **Core.**
   - Writer, row, settings, `HDR_ROWS`, layout and EBML as in Interfaces; the header. No format bump and no new `rc_*`.
   - Tests:
     - `export_vp9.rs`: the row JSON; the settings with `writer` and no `encoder_speed`; the speed refusal; HLG `hlg` by default with `pq`/`sdr` as asked; SDR refusals; even size.
     - `webm_writer_vp9.rs`: Profile 0 SDR and Profile 2 PQ layouts written, then re-read through `Container`. Check codec `V_VP9`, fourcc `vp09`, the synthesized `vpcC` profile and depth, no CodecPrivate in `common/ebml_read.rs`'s walk, the Colour codes, BitsPerChannel, the mastering metadata and the key flags.
     - Update the other listed tests: EXPECTED becomes 14 rows; the writer-key tests allow `writer` alone on `vp9_webm`; `EVEN_SIZED` gets 11 entries; six HDR rows.
3. **Calibration** (step 1.7) runs once the encoder works. Fill the table, then write the guide and catalog sentences naming VP9's measured maximum.
4. **Swift.**
   - The shim and the protocol come first. Then `SVTAV1Encoder` conformance, with `crf` going through `ExportRateTable`; this is a pure change, and P1 guards it.
   - Then `VP9Encoder`, the 8-bit kernel, and the pump choosing by writer.
   - Then the layout `VideoCodec`, the WebM writer's guard (`av1Writer` or `vp9Writer`), the sheet's `softCap` and `codecFactor`, and the catalog text.
5. **Proof: `vp9_export_proof.py`.**
   - Modelled on `webm_export_proof.py`, importing its helpers and `av1_export_proof.py`'s. Output goes to `work/vp9-export/`, and an instrument that cannot run is a FAIL.
   - Rows:
     - Z1: logs silent.
     - V1: A1's project. Expect `matroska,webm`; `vp9` Profile 0 `yuv420p` 640×360; Opus 48 kHz stereo; 5.0 s ± 1 frame. The walk finds V_VP9, no CodecPrivate, and Colour 1/1/1/Range 1/8.
     - V2: no `ffmpeg -v error` line; 150 frames; 240,000 samples.
     - V3: the first block is a key; key gaps ≤ 2 s; fewer keys than blocks. Each block's walk key flag equals "its first frame's VP9 header has show_existing 0 and frame_type 0", in both directions.
     - V4: SDR, `vp9_webm` against `hevc` at 20 Mb/s decoded as yuv420p. Per-plane MAD ≤ 6 over frames 0–149, and each stripes patch ≤ 3 codes.
     - V5: W5's chapters and W6's range (60 frames, 96,000 samples, chapters clamped).
     - V6: W9's cancel ends within 10 s and leaves no file.
     - V7: `encoder_speed` is refused with the sentence and leaves no file; the done answer has no `encoder_speed`.
     - V8: the HLG doc at default, `pq` and `sdr`. Check:
       - the answer's range;
       - profile 2/2/0 and `yuv420p10le`/`yuv420p10le`/`yuv420p`;
       - ffprobe tags; `trace_headers`' `color_space`;
       - the walk's Colour (9/18/9/10; 9/16/9/10 with MasteringMetadata and MaxCLL 1000/MaxFALL 0; 1/1/1/8);
       - PQ mastering side data at HD-5's values and no HDR side data on the others.
     - V9: hlg and pq against `hevc_10bit` as yuv420p10le: MAD ≤ 6 and stripes ≤ 4.

**Reported finding, not pinned.** H7w's two SDR WebMs (1024 × 128, BT.709 ×3) are now labelled where they were not. H7w compares them only with each other and still passes.

**Side observation.** A copy's ffprobe colour fields read BT.709 even without the label, from `vpcC` and the bitstream. That is why H7s's render check is the one that sees the label.

## What I did

- **Decision first.** CX-16 (1)–(10), with (8) the full calibration. The amendments under CX-8, CX-15, HD-5, HD-14 (c), HD-18 (b) and HD-19 (b); the index rows and Lines cells.
- **Core:**
  - `Writer::Libvpx` and `takes_speed`; the `vp9_webm` row (14 rows); `writer` and `encoder_speed` emitted as specified.
  - Six `HDR_ROWS` and the 8-bit sentence.
  - The layout's optional private, with the spec's four refusals.
  - `video_entry(codec_id, Option<private>)`, the header, and `stream_matrix`.
  - New tests: `export_vp9.rs` (6) and `webm_writer_vp9.rs` (5). The other listed tests are updated.
- **Swift:**
  - `FrameJobVPX.h`, `ExportVideoEncoder.swift` and `ExportVP9Encoder.swift` (238 lines).
  - SVT's conformance, with `crf` through `ExportRateTable` and unchanged values (P1 checks them).
  - The pump choosing by `writer`, `webmCodec`, the optional format description.
  - The I420 kernel and `bitDepth`, `cicp`, `VideoCodec`.
  - The writer guard, the sink's optional format, and `ExporterWriter`'s one identifier.
  - `ExportPreset.writer` and `softCap`, `codecFactor` for VP9, and the catalog descriptions.
  - The rewrap labels.
- **The CQ table**, from `crf_vp9.py`:
  - 8-bit is the lower of the spike half (34/30/26/24/16) and the owner half (34/26/20/18/14), giving **34/26/20/18/14**.
  - 10-bit is the owner clip in HLG against `hevc_10bit` at `hlg`: 34/28/26/24/20, then Format default lowered to 24 after Release R3, giving **34/28/24/24/20**.
  - The spike's largest cap share was 1.143 ×, and every kept owner file was under the cap.
  - No cell missed its comparator, so there was no product STOP. The guide, MCP page and catalog say "about 1.15".
- **Documents:**
  - Spec §7.1, §7.4, §7.7, §7.8, §7.9a and §7.10.
  - The guide's export, hdr-and-color, mcp and projects-and-media pages, and the README.
  - `docs/manual-checks.md`: SE-19, and HDR-2's and HDR-8's VP9 lines.
  - `tools/proof/README.md`'s C4 section, and the `designs/codec-export.md` "## C4" record. The record includes RULING-1, every measurement and the "CLAUDE.md edits owed".
- **Proofs:**
  - `vp9_export_proof.py` (Z1, V1–V11, S1, P1, R1–R3, ten mutants) and `vp9_rate_probe.swift`.
  - E41 and E42 in `export_offset_proof.py`.
  - H7s in `hdr_proof.py`.
  - The sentence constants in `av1_export_proof.py`, `hdr_proof.py` and `hevc_alpha_proof.py`.
  - `av1-not-hdr` re-anchored; it was re-run and caught.

## Deviations, each with its reason

- **Mutant rows** (RULING-1 accepted the first three):
  - `sdr-at-10-bits` names V1 **and V8**: V8's `sdr` case reads the same profile and depth.
  - `transfer-unlabelled` mutates only the HLG and PQ transfers in `ExportAV1Picture.cicp`. Mutating every transfer would fail V1's SDR Colour too. It stays V8 alone.
  - `speed-on-vp9` mutates `Preset::takes_encoder_speed` back to `writer.is_some()` and names V7, **S1** and cargo `export_vp9`. The settings' speed becomes the footnote's "· Balanced", which S1 reads.
  - `all-key` names V3 **and V10**. Measured: the copy marks every sample a sync sample, so the render at 3 s decodes an inter frame as a key (R/G/B ≈ 125/255). Its first run was `CAUGHT, NOT EXACTLY`; with V10 added it exited 1.
  - **A tenth mutant**, `sdr-copy-unlabelled` (V10), was added by RULING-1.
- **The spike half of the calibration** is scored against each clip's y4m source. That is the reference `crf.jsonl`'s spike HEVC rows were scored against; the spike clips never went through the app, so they have no `prores_422`.
- **VMAF pairs frames by index** (`settb=1/30,setpts=N`) in the calibration and the R rows. A WebM's whole-millisecond block times made libvmaf's timestamp pairing compare a third of the frames against neighbours: 76.17 where index pairing reads about 91. The rows from that bad run stay in `crf.jsonl` without `"align": "index"`, and are ignored.
- **The 10-bit Format default cell is 24, not the first calibration's 26.**
  - Release R3 met a `hevc_10bit` encode at 95.692, against the calibration's 95.620; `vp9_webm` at CQ 26 scored 95.679.
  - By CX-16 (7)'s rule I lowered the cell by 2, to CQ 24, already measured at 95.958 (0.893 × the cap).
  - Recorded in CX-16 (8) and the C4 record. This is the same VideoToolbox variance C2 saw.
- **Small changes:**
  - `ExportI010Converter`'s failure sentences say "the encoder" rather than "the AV1 encoder".
  - Its `bitDepth` defaults to 10, so `webm_readers_probe.swift` builds unchanged.
  - `ExportEncodePump`'s out-of-order sentence names the encoder. AV1's text is unchanged.

## Files touched outside the spec's Files list, and why

- `core/src/container_codec.rs`, `core/src/container.rs`, `app/Sources/ContainerRewrap.swift`, `app/Sources/ContainerRewrapWriter.swift`, `core/tests/common/webm.rs` (`vp9_frame_in`) and `core/tests/webm_writer_vp9.rs`'s stream-matrix test: RULING-1's fix.
- `designs/spec/07.7-import.md` and `docs/guide/projects-and-media.md`: the import's user-visible colour change, which the guide rule requires.

## Still failing / owed

- **`hdr_proof.py` H7i** cannot run its byte half on this host: there is no control capture. The rest of it held. This is not caused by this change.
- **Not run:** `webm_export_proof.py`, `av1_export_proof.py`, `hdr_proof.py --only DR,Z1` and `hevc_alpha_proof.py` were not re-run after the final table edit. That edit touches only `VP9Encoder`'s table, which none of them reads; the `vp9_export_proof.py --rate` re-run covers it.
- **Owner's manual checks:** SE-19, and HDR-8's VP9 half.
- **CLAUDE.md edits for the integrator** are listed in the C4 record.

1	# Spec: codec-export C4 — VP9 (libvpx) in WebM, 8-bit SDR and Profile 2 HDR (#377)
2	
3	## Goal
4	Add a `vp9_webm` export row: libvpx v1.17.0 (good, cpu-used 4, row-mt; CX-3) encoding into the core's WebM writer with C3's Opus, silent movie, chapters, range and #337 length. It is Profile 0 8-bit for an SDR picture and Profile 2 10-bit for HLG/PQ, with the container's Colour carrying the transfer and HD-5's HDR10. The rate is capped constant quality calibrated against `hevc` / `hevc_10bit`.
5	
6	## Files
7	Worktree `~/devel/framejob-codecs` (branch `codecs`). Never commit.
8	- `designs/spec/11-decisions/codec-export.md`: CX-16 (below), written BEFORE any code. "Amended by CX-16" lines under CX-8 and CX-15 (1)–(3).
9	- `designs/spec/11-decisions/hdr.md`: "Amended by CX-16" under HD-5's row list (line ~168) and HD-14 (c) (line ~478). There are now six HDR rows and the new sentence.
10	- `designs/spec/11-decisions/README.md`: the file row's text and line count, plus a CX-16 row. `designs/spec/README.md`: the Lines cells.
11	- `designs/spec/07.8-export.md`, `07.1-ffi-surface.md` (webm layout comment), `07.4-swift-file-map.md`, `07.10-rust-module-map.md`, `07.9a-agent-tools.md`: the row, the writer, V_VP9.
12	- `designs/codec-export.md`: a "## C4" record shaped like C3's: decision, what landed, commands and output, calibration, findings, "CLAUDE.md edits owed", owed.
13	- `core/src/export_encoder.rs`: `Writer::Libvpx` and `Writer::takes_speed`.
14	- `core/src/export_table.rs`: the `vp9_webm` row; `takes_encoder_speed`; `to_json` (`writer` on every writer row, `encoder_speeds` only where speeds apply).
15	- `core/src/export.rs`: settings emit `writer` for every writer row and `encoder_speed` only where speeds apply; the module doc.
16	- `core/src/dynamic_range.rs`: `HDR_ROWS` has six entries, and the 8-bit sentence names `vp9_webm`.
17	- `core/src/webm_layout.rs`: accepts `V_VP9`, makes the private optional, and checks the depth.

76	   1. The row as Interfaces says. It is even-sized, an HDR row, and `optimize_for_network` has no effect on it.
77	   2. **One speed (CX-3 binds).** cpu-used 4, `VPX_DL_GOOD_QUALITY`, row-mt. There is no `encoder_speeds`, and the Speed popup is disabled on this row. The request's "Speed popup mapped to cpu-used" is not built because it would re-litigate CX-3.
78	   3. **Depth by picture.** `sdr` (an SDR project, or `sdr` asked) is Profile 0 (`g_profile` 0), 8-bit I420, BT.709. `hlg` and `pq` are Profile 2, 10-bit I010, BT.2020 NCL, with `g_profile` 2, `VPX_CODEC_USE_HIGHBITDEPTH`, `g_bit_depth`/`g_input_bit_depth` 10 and `VPX_IMG_FMT_I42016` (libvpx's `validate_config` refuses a depth above 8 at a profile below 2). Reason: Profile 0 is VP9's universal decode profile, VP9's purpose is web playback (CX-3), and unlike AV1 Main (CX-14 (1)) Profile 0 cannot carry 10 bits. The 8-bit samples are Y = round(16 + 219·Y′) and C = clamp(round(128 + 224·C′), 0, 255), where C′ is the mean of its 2×2 block and the matrix is as CX-14 (3).

3	/// libvpx v1.17.0's VP9, the `vp9_webm` row's encoder (spec §11 CX-3, CX-4, CX-16): one context
4	/// per export, configured once, fed video-range pictures and drained of packets.
5	///
6	/// **Owned by one serial queue.** `ExportEncodePump`'s encode queue makes every call after
7	/// `init` — `send`, `sendEndOfStream`, `nextPacket` and the `deinit` — so the context is never
8	/// touched from two threads; libvpx runs its own worker threads (`g_threads`, row-mt) behind
9	/// it.
10	///
11	/// **The configuration** (CX-16 (2)–(7)): `VPX_DL_GOOD_QUALITY` at cpu-used 4 with row-mt, the
12	/// one speed (CX-3); the depth by picture — Profile 0, 8-bit I420 for `sdr`, Profile 2, 10-bit
13	/// I010 (`VPX_IMG_FMT_I42016`) for `hlg` and `pq` — with the matrix's colour space in studio
14	/// range; a keyframe at least every 2 s (`kf_max_dist` ⌊2·fps⌋); a 25-frame lag with alt-refs,
15	/// two log2 tile columns; and capped constant quality: `VPX_CQ` at the table's CQ level with
16	/// the cap as the target, libvpx's own 25 % overshoot. VP9's bitstream carries no transfer, so
17	/// the WebM `Colour` is the picture's only label (`ExportWebMLayout`).
18	///
19	/// **Packets.** libvpx packs a hidden alt-ref into the next shown frame's superframe, so each
20	/// packet is one shown frame at the pts (the frame index, timebase 1/fps) it was sent with.
21	/// They are collected after each `vpx_codec_encode` into `pending`; the end of stream encodes
22	/// NULL until no packet comes out.
23	final class VP9Encoder: ExportVideoEncoder {
24	    let name = "libvpx"
25	
26	    private var context = vpx_codec_ctx_t()
27	    private var image = vpx_image_t()
28	    private var open = false
29	    private let format: vpx_img_fmt_t
30	    private let bytesPerSample: Int
31	    private let bitDepth: Int
32	    /// The packets libvpx has answered and the pump has not yet taken, oldest first.
33	    private var pending: [ExportEncodedPacket] = []
34	    private var flushing = false
35	    private var drained = false
36	    /// Set after the first failed call: nothing more is asked of the context but its teardown.
37	    private var broken = false
38	
39	    init(width: Int, height: Int, fps: Fps, bitsPerSecond: Int, picture: ExportAV1Picture) throws {
40	        let depth = Self.bitDepth(for: picture)
41	        bitDepth = depth
42	        bytesPerSample = depth > 8 ? 2 : 1
43	        format = depth > 8 ? VPX_IMG_FMT_I42016 : VPX_IMG_FMT_I420
44	        var config = vpx_codec_enc_cfg_t()
45	        try Self.check(
46	            vpx_codec_enc_config_default(vpx_codec_vp9_cx(), &config, 0),
47	            "vpx_codec_enc_config_default", context: nil)
48	        config.g_w = UInt32(clamping: width)
49	        config.g_h = UInt32(clamping: height)
50	        // Timebase 1/fps: a frame's pts is its index and its duration 1.
51	        config.g_timebase = vpx_rational(
52	            num: Int32(clamping: max(1, fps.den)), den: Int32(clamping: max(1, fps.num)))
53	        config.g_threads = UInt32(clamping: ProcessInfo.processInfo.activeProcessorCount)
54	        config.g_pass = VPX_RC_ONE_PASS
55	        config.g_lag_in_frames = 25
56	        // The depth (CX-16 (3)): libvpx's `validate_config` refuses a depth above 8 at a
57	        // profile below 2.
58	        config.g_profile = depth > 8 ? 2 : 0
59	        config.g_bit_depth = depth > 8 ? VPX_BITS_10 : VPX_BITS_8
60	        config.g_input_bit_depth = UInt32(depth)
61	        // Capped CQ (CX-16 (7)): the cap in kb/s as the target, libvpx's default
62	        // over- and undershoot (25 / 25).
63	        let cap = max(1, bitsPerSecond)
64	        config.rc_end_usage = VPX_CQ
65	        config.rc_target_bitrate = UInt32(max(1, (Double(cap) / 1000).rounded()))
66	        // A keyframe at least every 2 s (CX-16 (6)).
67	        let perSecond = fps.den > 0 ? Double(fps.num) / Double(fps.den) : 30
68	        config.kf_mode = VPX_KF_AUTO
69	        config.kf_min_dist = 0
70	        config.kf_max_dist = UInt32(max(1, (2 * perSecond).rounded(.down)))
71	        let flags = depth > 8 ? vpx_codec_flags_t(VPX_CODEC_USE_HIGHBITDEPTH) : 0
72	        try Self.check(
73	            framejob_vpx_vp9_enc_init(&context, &config, flags), "vpx_codec_enc_init",
74	            context: nil)
75	        open = true
76	        let pixels = Double(max(1, width * height)) * (perSecond > 0 ? perSecond : 30)
77	        let controls: [(vp8e_enc_control_id, Int32)] = [
78	            (VP8E_SET_CPUUSED, 4),
79	            (VP9E_SET_ROW_MT, 1),
80	            (VP8E_SET_ENABLEAUTOALTREF, 1),
81	            (VP9E_SET_TILE_COLUMNS, 2),
82	            (VP9E_SET_FRAME_PARALLEL_DECODING, 0),
83	            (VP8E_SET_CQ_LEVEL,
84	             Int32(Self.cqLevel(bitDepth: depth, bitsPerPixel: Double(cap) / pixels))),
85	            (VP9E_SET_COLOR_SPACE,
86	             Int32((picture == .sdr ? VPX_CS_BT_709 : VPX_CS_BT_2020).rawValue)),
87	            (VP9E_SET_COLOR_RANGE, Int32(VPX_CR_STUDIO_RANGE.rawValue)),
88	        ]
89	        for (id, value) in controls {
90	            try Self.check(
91	                framejob_vpx_control_int(&context, Int32(id.rawValue), value),
92	                "vpx_codec_control \(id.rawValue)", context: &context)
93	        }
94	        // The image header `send` points at each frame's planes: 4:2:0 at the export size,
95	        // the picture's colour space in studio range (no storage of its own).
96	        image.fmt = format
97	        image.cs = picture == .sdr ? VPX_CS_BT_709 : VPX_CS_BT_2020
98	        image.range = VPX_CR_STUDIO_RANGE
99	        image.w = UInt32(clamping: width)
100	        image.h = UInt32(clamping: height)
101	        image.d_w = image.w
102	        image.d_h = image.h
103	        image.bit_depth = UInt32(depth)
104	        image.x_chroma_shift = 1
105	        image.y_chroma_shift = 1
106	        image.bps = depth > 8 ? 24 : 12
107	    }

109	    @available(*, unavailable) required init?(coder: NSCoder) {
110	        fatalError("VP9Encoder does not support NSCoder")
111	    }

113	    deinit {
114	        if open { _ = vpx_codec_destroy(&context) }
115	    }
116	
117	    /// The picture's depth (CX-16 (3)): 8 for the SDR picture, 10 for HLG and PQ.
118	    static func bitDepth(for picture: ExportAV1Picture) -> Int {
119	        picture == .sdr ? 8 : 10
120	    }
121	
122	    /// VP9's packets go into the WebM as libvpx wrote them.
123	    func containerBytes(_ data: Data) throws -> Data {
124	        data
125	    }
126	
127	    /// Sends one picture; libvpx copies its planes into its lookahead, so `frame` may be reused
128	    /// once this returns. Strides go in bytes, the planes where the converter put them.
129	    func send(_ frame: I010Frame, index: Int64) throws {
130	        guard open, !broken, !flushing else { throw Self.stopped }
131	        guard frame.bitDepth == bitDepth else {
132	            throw Exporter.ExportError.failed(
133	                "libvpx failed: a \(frame.bitDepth)-bit frame was sent to a \(bitDepth)-bit encoder.")
134	        }
135	        let base = frame.buffer.contents().assumingMemoryBound(to: UInt8.self)
136	        image.planes.0 = base
137	        image.planes.1 = base + bytesPerSample * frame.cbOffset
138	        image.planes.2 = base + bytesPerSample * frame.crOffset
139	        image.stride.0 = Int32(bytesPerSample * frame.lumaStride)
140	        image.stride.1 = Int32(bytesPerSample * frame.chromaStride)
141	        image.stride.2 = Int32(bytesPerSample * frame.chromaStride)
142	        try record(
143	            vpx_codec_encode(&context, &image, index, 1, 0, UInt(VPX_DL_GOOD_QUALITY)),
144	            "vpx_codec_encode")
145	        collect()
146	    }
147	
148	    /// No picture follows: `nextPacket(wait: true)` encodes NULL until libvpx answers nothing.
149	    func sendEndOfStream() throws {
150	        guard open, !broken else { throw Self.stopped }
151	        flushing = true
152	    }
153	
154	    /// The next packet: the oldest pending one. `wait` true, after `sendEndOfStream`, flushes
155	    /// libvpx until a packet comes out or none is left, then answers nil.
156	    func nextPacket(wait: Bool) throws -> ExportEncodedPacket? {
157	        guard open, !broken else { throw Self.stopped }
158	        while pending.isEmpty, wait, flushing, !drained {
159	            try record(
160	                vpx_codec_encode(&context, nil, 0, 1, 0, UInt(VPX_DL_GOOD_QUALITY)),
161	                "vpx_codec_encode")
162	            if !collect() { drained = true }
163	        }
164	        return pending.isEmpty ? nil : pending.removeFirst()
165	    }
166	
167	    /// Every frame packet libvpx has ready into `pending`; whether there was one.
168	    @discardableResult
169	    private func collect() -> Bool {
170	        var iterator: vpx_codec_iter_t?
171	        var any = false
172	        while let packet = vpx_codec_get_cx_data(&context, &iterator) {
173	            guard packet.pointee.kind == VPX_CODEC_CX_FRAME_PKT else { continue }
174	            let frame = packet.pointee.data.frame
175	            let data = frame.buf.map { Data(bytes: $0, count: frame.sz) } ?? Data()
176	            pending.append(ExportEncodedPacket(
177	                data: data, pts: frame.pts, isLast: false,
178	                isKey: frame.flags & vpx_codec_frame_flags_t(VPX_FRAME_IS_KEY) != 0))

180	        }

194	        (0.0579, [8: 26, 10: 28]),
195	        (0.0700, [8: 20, 10: 24]),
196	        (0.0772, [8: 18, 10: 24]),
197	        (0.1157, [8: 14, 10: 20]),

+++ b/designs/spec/11-decisions/codec-export.md
+  **Amended by CX-16** (C4): `vp9_webm` is Profile 0 8-bit for an SDR picture and Profile 2
+  10-bit for HLG and PQ, the WebM `Colour` the only transfer label, with HD-5's HDR10 on PQ.
+  **Amended by CX-16** (C4): (1)'s neighbour `vp9_webm` follows `av1_webm`, an HDR row with
+  `writer` `libvpx` and no speeds; (2)'s `ExportWebMWriter` writes it too, its pump choosing the
+  encoder by `writer`; and (3)'s Track 1 is `V_AV1` with its `av1C` or `V_VP9` with no
+  CodecPrivate, BitsPerChannel 10 on AV1 and 8 or 10 on VP9 by the picture.
+
+- **CX-16 — C4: `vp9_webm`, 8-bit Profile 0 for SDR and 10-bit Profile 2 for HLG and PQ**
+  (default, recorded in C4 before its code; amends CX-8, CX-15 (1)–(3), HD-5 and HD-14 (c)):
+  1. **The row.** `vp9_webm` is "VP9 (WebM)", directly after `av1_webm`: container `webm`,
+     codec `vp9`, video, no alpha (alpha is C5's row), `size` and `fps` null, `avf_preset`
+     `AVAssetExportPresetPassthrough` (a record, as on `av1_webm`), `"hdr": true` and `writer`
+     `libvpx`, with no `encoder_speeds`. It is even-sized, one of HD-5's HDR rows, and
+     `optimize_for_network` has no effect on it. Its settings carry `writer` (`libvpx`) and
+     no `encoder_speed`; `color` in an HLG project as every HDR row's.
+  2. **One speed (CX-3 binds).** libvpx runs `VPX_DL_GOOD_QUALITY` at cpu-used 4 with row-mt.
+     There is no `encoder_speeds`, `encoder_speed` on the row is refused with the existing
+     sentence (`vp9_webm has no encoder speed; encoder_speed applies to av1 and av1_webm`), and
+     the sheet's Speed popup is drawn disabled on it, as on every row without speeds. The
+     brief's "Speed popup mapped to cpu-used" is not built: it would re-litigate CX-3.
+  3. **The depth is the picture's.** `sdr` (an SDR project, or `sdr` asked in an HLG project)
+     is Profile 0 (`g_profile` 0): 8-bit I420, BT.709. `hlg` and `pq` are Profile 2: 10-bit
+     I010, BT.2020 non-constant, with `g_profile` 2, `VPX_CODEC_USE_HIGHBITDEPTH`,
+     `g_bit_depth` and `g_input_bit_depth` 10 and `VPX_IMG_FMT_I42016` (libvpx's
+     `validate_config` refuses a depth above 8 at a profile below 2). WHY: Profile 0 is VP9's
+     universal decode profile, VP9's reason to be on the sheet is web playback (CX-3), and
+     unlike AV1's Main profile (CX-14 (1)) Profile 0 cannot carry 10 bits, so an always-10-bit
+     row would be a Profile 2 file for every SDR export. The 8-bit samples are CX-14 (3)'s
+     arithmetic at 8 bits: Y = round(16 + 219·Y′) and each chroma sample
+     clamp(round(128 + 224·C′), 0, 255), C′ the mean of its 2 × 2 block, the matrix BT.709's.
+  4. **The tags.** libvpx's `VP9E_SET_COLOR_SPACE` is `VPX_CS_BT_709` or `VPX_CS_BT_2020` and
+     `VP9E_SET_COLOR_RANGE` studio. VP9's bitstream carries no transfer function, so the WebM
+     `Colour` is the only transfer label (CX-8): the picture's CICP (`sdr` 1/1/1, `hlg` 9/18/9,
+     `pq` 9/16/9), Range 1 and BitsPerChannel 8 or 10; on PQ alone it also carries HD-5's
+     MasteringMetadata, MaxCLL and MaxFALL from `OutputTransform`'s two blobs, as CX-15 (3)
+     writes them for `av1_webm`.
+  5. **No CodecPrivate.** Matroska's VP9 mapping makes it optional, ffmpeg writes none, and
+     #216-R's reader builds `vpcC` from the first keyframe, so the TrackEntry is `V_VP9` with
+     none. The layout's `codec_private_hex` becomes optional: required and non-empty on `V_AV1`,
+     refused on `V_VP9`; `bits_per_channel` is checked to be 8 or 10.
+  6. **Keys and packets.** `kf_mode` auto, `kf_min_dist` 0 and `kf_max_dist` ⌊2·fps⌋ (a
+     keyframe at least every 2 s, as CX-12 (3)); the block's key flag is libvpx's
+     `VPX_FRAME_IS_KEY`. `g_lag_in_frames` 25, auto-alt-ref 1, `VP9E_SET_TILE_COLUMNS` 2,
+     frame-parallel decoding 0, `g_threads` the active processor count; timebase 1/fps, a
+     frame's pts its index, duration 1. libvpx packs a hidden alt-ref into the next shown
+     frame's superframe, so each packet is one shown frame at its pts. A libvpx failure reads
+     "libvpx failed: <step> answered <code>: <detail>", and one before the first frame "libvpx
+     could not start: …".
+  7. **The rate: capped constant quality, quality first** (CX-13's model). `rc_end_usage` is
+     `VPX_CQ`, `VP8E_SET_CQ_LEVEL` the table's value and `rc_target_bitrate` the cap in kb/s
+     (rounded, at least 1), the cap CX-13 (2)'s: `video_bitrate` when asked (the Quality tiers'
+     0.6 factor, CX-9 (2)), else HEVC's 0.07 bits per pixel per frame. `rc_overshoot_pct` and
+     `rc_undershoot_pct` stay at libvpx's defaults (25 / 25), as CX-13 took SVT's own. The CQ
+     level is a function of the cap's bits per pixel per frame and the depth: linear between
+     CX-13's five points, rounded down, the end point's beyond either end. The 8-bit column is
+     the lower of two calibrations: (a) the spike's gh5, promo and real8 through the spike's
+     `vpxenc` (`--end-usage=cq`, the flags above, CQ 10–50 in steps of 2) against `crf.jsonl`'s
+     HEVC rows, and (b) the owner's IMG_0018.MOV in an SDR project through a Release copy
+     reading the CQ from a file, against `hevc`, both scored against `prores_422` as yuv420p.
+     The 10-bit column is the owner clip in an HLG project at `hlg`, against `hevc_10bit` at
+     `hlg`, scored as yuv420p10le. Each cell is the highest CQ reaching at least the
+     comparator's VMAF under the real cap; a cell that misses is lowered by 2 until it meets
+     the comparator or the cap binds. The measurements are (8).
+  8. **The calibration** (`tools/proof/work/codec-spike/crf_vp9.py`, gitignored; rows `kind`
+     "vpx" in `crf.jsonl`), 2026-10-28 on a shared machine. VMAF pairs the two files' frames
+     by INDEX (`settb=1/30,setpts=N`): a WebM's block times are whole milliseconds, and
+     libvmaf's timestamp pairing put a third of the owner clip's frames against a neighbour's
+     (the first owner run read 76.17 at CQ 30 / Low where index pairing reads about 91; its
+     rows lack `"align": "index"` and are not used). Each VMAF below is "CQ: VMAF (share of
+     the cap)", the kept cell in bold.
+     - **(a) The spike's clips** (vpxenc, 8-bit, against `crf.jsonl`'s spike HEVC rows,
+       scored against each clip's own y4m as those rows were; a search of the grid, 81
+       encodes): cells gh5 / promo / real8 — Low 46 / 34 / 36, Medium 38 / 30 / 30, Format
+       default 34 / 30 / 26, High 32 / 30 / 24, Maximum 28 / 28 / 16. The largest cap share
+       of the 81 was **1.143 ×** (gh5 at Low, at CQ 10 and 30, where the cap binds).
+     - **(b) The owner's clip at 8 bits** (an SDR project, `vp9_webm` against `hevc` —
+       91.141 / 94.415 / 95.469 / 95.777 / 96.85 — both against its `prores_422` as
+       yuv420p): Low 36: 90.871 (0.712), **34: 91.568 (0.786)**; Medium 32: 92.880, 30:
+       93.664, 28: 94.081, **26: 94.431 (0.867)**; Format default 30: 93.874, 28: 94.367,
+       26: 94.811, 24: 95.215, 22: 95.375, **20: 95.498 (0.938)**; High 30: 93.957 … 20:
+       95.753, **18: 95.882 (0.948)**; Maximum 26: 95.248 … 16: 96.844, **14: 96.993
+       (0.912)**.
+     - **(c) The owner's clip at 10 bits** (an HLG project at `hlg`, against `hevc_10bit` at
+       `hlg` — 92.064 / 94.681 / 95.620 / 95.976 / 97.133 — scored as yuv420p10le): Low
+       36: 91.907 (0.786), **34: 92.455 (0.852)**; Medium 30: 94.571 (0.790), **28: 94.897
+       (0.848)**, 26: 95.164 (0.904); Format default 28: 95.316 (0.748), 26: 95.679
+       (0.825), **24: 95.958 (0.893)** (kept after R3, below), 22: 96.066, 20: 96.145
+       (0.948); High 26: 95.868 (0.775),
+       **24: 96.198 (0.855)**, 22: 96.338, 20: 96.435, 18: 96.499 (0.946); Maximum 22:
+       97.038 (0.700), **20: 97.234 (0.754)**, 18: 97.393, 16: 97.508, 14: 97.578 (0.890).
+
+     | bits per pixel per frame (the 1080p30 rate) | 8-bit (Profile 0) | 10-bit (Profile 2) |
+     |---|---|---|
+     | 0.0386 (Low, 2.4 Mb/s) | 34 | 34 |
+     | 0.0579 (Medium, 3.6 Mb/s) | 26 | 28 |
+     | 0.0700 (Format default, 4.35 Mb/s) | 20 | 24 |
+     | 0.0772 (High, 4.8 Mb/s) | 18 | 24 |
+     | 0.1157 (Maximum, 7.2 Mb/s) | 14 | 20 |
+
+     The owner's clip binds every 8-bit point (the spike's cells are 34 / 30 / 26 / 24 /
+     16); every cell reached its comparator under the real cap, so no STOP. The guide, the
+     MCP page and `video_bitrate`'s description name the measured maximum as about 1.15 ×
+     the cap. The least margins kept: 8-bit Medium +0.016, Format default +0.029.
+     **The 10-bit Format default cell was lowered from 26 to 24 at the first `--rate` run**
+     (`vp9_export_proof.py` R3 on Release): that run's `hevc_10bit` Format default encode
+     scored 95.692 (the calibration's, 95.620) and `vp9_webm` at CQ 26 the calibration's
+     95.679, 0.013 under; by (7)'s rule the cell went down by 2, to the CQ 24 the
+     calibration had measured at 95.958 (0.893 × the cap), +0.27 over either comparator. C2
+     saw the same one-encode variance in VideoToolbox's `hevc_10bit` (CX-14 (6)).
+  9. **The C wrappers.** `vpx_codec_enc_init` is a macro and `vpx_codec_control_` is variadic,
+     neither of which Swift can call, so `app/Bridging/FrameJobVPX.h` wraps them in two
